Composition Science Research

Phase 2: Visual Hierarchy, Wayfinding, and Attention

Purpose

The next phase shifts from studying architecture as physical space to understanding how humans allocate attention and construct mental models.

Central question:

How do humans know where to look?

Core Hypothesis

Composition is the external organization of information to match the internal operating characteristics of the human brain.

Research Areas

Attention

  • Contrast
  • Size
  • Motion
  • Novelty
  • Faces
  • Text
  • Color
  • Orientation

Research:

  • What attracts attention first?
  • What causes attention to shift?
  • What interrupts attention?

Eye Movement

Topics:

  • Saccades
  • Fixations
  • Scan paths
  • Peripheral vision
  • Visual search

Questions:

  • Can eye movements be predicted?
  • Can layouts reduce unnecessary eye movement?

Landmarks

Variables:

  • Uniqueness
  • Contrast
  • Location
  • Frequency
  • Size
  • Isolation

Mental Maps

Study how people build internal representations of environments and information.

Decision Points

Variables:

  • Number of choices
  • Uncertainty
  • Visibility
  • Reversibility
  • Familiarity

Hierarchy

Hierarchy includes:

  • Position
  • Isolation
  • Contrast
  • Motion
  • Size
  • White space
  • Timing
  • Color
  • Shape
  • Repetition

Predictability

Investigate how expectation guides navigation and how violations of expectation affect comprehension.

Emerging Cross-Domain Laws

LAW-COMP-001: Attention flows toward the highest information gain for the lowest expected cost.

LAW-COMP-002: Distinct landmarks reduce navigation uncertainty.

LAW-COMP-003: Navigation succeeds when local decisions reinforce a coherent global mental model.

LAW-COMP-004: Visual hierarchy is fundamentally an attention allocation mechanism.

LAW-COMP-005: Every unnecessary decision consumes cognitive capacity that cannot be used for the primary task.

Broader Theory

Composition is fundamentally about managing limited cognitive resources:

  • Attention
  • Working memory
  • Visual processing
  • Decision making
  • Prediction
  • Anticipated effort
  • Emotion

Next Investigation

Perform a comprehensive review of:

  1. Eye-tracking research
  2. Visual search
  3. Saliency models
  4. Cognitive psychology
  5. Neuroscience of attention
  6. Wayfinding
  7. Human-computer interaction

Goal:

Identify measurable variables that recur across disciplines and convert them into evidence-backed composition laws.
